key_insight: Natural policy gradient achieves near-minimax-optimal transition-query complexity of Õ(SAH⁴/ε²), with a matching Ω(SAH⁴/ε²) lower bound and guarantees for the final policy.
engineering_relevance: Direct policy optimization can reach fundamental sampling limits in tabular finite-horizon reinforcement learning without explicitly estimating transition probabilities.
method: Study known-reward MDPs with unknown, horizon-dependent transitions accessed through a generative model.
Update policies through backward-sweep natural policy gradient under three batch-size and step-size schedules.
Prove last-iterate upper bounds and an information-theoretic lower bound covering adaptive queries.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees rather than empirical benchmarks, including an Ω(H²/ε) worst-case iteration lower bound for exact NPG with known kernels and step size 1/H.
watch_item: The guarantees assume tabular MDPs, known rewards, and generative-model access; they do not establish equivalent performance with function approximation or online-only interaction.
paper_title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
